findings.explanation: Not a real gap for this repo. The module is versioned independently via semver git tags (source = "JamesWoolfenden/cloud-armour/gcp", consumers pin a module version), which is the actual compatibility contract. Adding required_providers to the module root would layer a second, uncoordinated provider constraint on top of that — one that can conflict with whatever the consuming root or sibling modules already declare (Terraform's classic nested-module version-constraint diamond problem) — for no real benefit, since a lock file inside a module directory is never read by Terraform at all (only the root configuration's lock file is used at init). Deliberately rejected by the module author; do not re-flag this pattern for reusable module roots in this author's repos.
findings.remediation: None — intentional design. Reusable modules stay unpinned at the root; only example/ (a deployable root config) gets required_version/required_providers and a lock file.
findings.title: Root module declares no required_providers / required_version constraint

findings.explanation: The variable description lists enforce_on_key values as IP, ALL, HTTP_HEADER, XFF_IP, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_PATH, SNI, REGION_CODE, but no validation block enforces this — unlike action and priority on the same variable, which both have validation. A typo (e.g. "Ip" or "HTTP_Header") passes terraform plan and only fails against the live GCP API at apply time. Checked against the current hashicorp/google provider source: the actual accepted set is larger than what's documented — it also includes TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, and USER_IP — so the description itself is out of date in addition to being unenforced.
findings.remediation: Add a validation block on rate_limit_rules constraining enforce_on_key to the full, current enum, and update the description to match.
findings.title: rate_limit_rules.enforce_on_key has no validation against its documented enum, and the documented enum is stale
